newsitem.title: JAPAN: FCC chief says BT-MCI merger to fuel competition.
newsitem.headline: FCC chief says BT-MCI merger to fuel competition.

text.p: The top phone regulator in the United States said on Wednesday that a planned merger between British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp would fuel competition in the U.S. local call market.

"We generally believe that the merger could very much strengthen the possibility that MCI would compete in the local market," said Reed Hundt, chairman of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which is now examining the planned merger.
He added, however, that the FCC is concerned about the merged company's marketing in Britain. He did not elaborate.
The comments were made at a meeting with an influential Japanese business group, the Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren).

Hundt reiterated his stance that he is opposed to a possible merger between AT&T Corp and SBC Communications Inc. He said AT&T potentially represents a powerful competitor in the local market and SBC, in the long-distance and international market.
"Neither of those possibilities of real competition would be achieved if the merger were permitted," Hundt said.

Earlier this week, Hundt met with the Japanese government and corporate officials and made clear his position that the FCC will not grant U.S. licences to Japan's two leading carriers until a bilateral dispute over foreign ownership restrictions is resolved.
U.S. officials have called on Japan to scrap a 20 percent ceiling on foreign ownership of of both Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) and Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co (KDD).
Hundt told reporters the FCC will not approve or disapprove the applications by NTT and KDD unless Japanese government officials confer with the U.S. trade office over the dispute.
Tokyo has said it would not start negotiations with the U.S. trade office unless the licencing and foreign ownership issues are separated.
